training-data.t: **Eight houses** are available for building the model (training and validation houses together). The **two test houses stay locked away**.

create-folds.t: Deal the eight houses into **four folds of two houses** each. Every house belongs to **exactly one** fold.

fold-one-validation.t: Fit the model on **folds 2, 3 and 4** (gold), then score it on **fold 1** (blue), which it never saw: validation MSE **0.0264**.

rotate.t: Round 2 makes **fold 2** the validation fold. The other three folds train a **fresh model**.

fold-two.t: Fit on folds 1, 3 and 4, then score on fold 2: validation MSE **0.0004**.

continue-rotating.t: Rounds 3 and 4 do the same with folds 3 and 4: validation MSE **0.0252 and 0.0914**. Now **every house has been used for validation exactly once**.

collect-scores.t: Four scores: **0.0264, 0.0004, 0.0252, 0.0914**. Their spread shows how much the result depends on **which houses were held out**.

average-score.t: The cross-validation score is the average: **(0.0264 + 0.0004 + 0.0252 + 0.0914) / 4 = 0.0359**. This is one steadier estimate for the straight line.

model-selection.t: Run the same procedure for other candidates and compare averages: the **line (0.0359)** beats the unregularized curve (**0.3169**) and the ridge curve with λ = 0.3 (**0.1662**). Then refit the winner on all development data. The folds are **not** the test set, which stays locked.
